clue.text: University courses here are famous

parts.note: read as both a seat of learning and a home of celebrated golf links in Fife, Scotland

explanation.surface: A boast about a university's renowned degree programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests degree programmes, but the famous courses here are golf courses: the town in Fife is the home of golf and of Scotland's oldest university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish town holds both an ancient university and the world's most celebrated golf links.

clue.text: Rest period for sailor in southern city

indicators.note: the sailor is placed inside the southern city, between its two parts

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's shore leave spent in a city in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly day of rest in Jewish and Christian tradition is a holy period of rest from work.

clue.text: Badly sited, in other words

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something poorly located, put another way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation i.e. means 'that is', a phrase used to restate something differently.

clue.text: See how the land lies, as rustlers do

definitions.meaning: to assess a situation before acting
cattle thieves literally make off with livestock

explanation.surface: Surveying the territory, the way cattle thieves would.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to review a situation, while cattle thieves literally seize farm animals.

clue.text: Mean approach

explanation.surface: A two-word phrase about an average way in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means tight-fisted in old usage and also, as a verb, to draw close.

clue.text: Author depicts giant's destruction after Jack climbs up

indicators.note: the scrambled giant follows the sailor's piece
in a down clue, climbing up reads the sailor's word from bottom to top

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, a tar

indicators.note: destroying the word giant breaks its letters up for reassembly

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A writer portrays a giant being destroyed after Jack climbs the beanstalk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbs up' turns TAR into RAT; 'destruction' rearranges GIANT into TIGAN. Terence Rattigan was an English playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was a twentieth-century English playwright, so a writer.

clue.text: Beat one in school

definitions.meaning: a school is a group of sea mammals swimming together

explanation.surface: A teacher punishing a pupil in a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To whale is an old verb for thrash, and these great cetaceans travel in groups called schools.

clue.text: After special plea, high-jumper's bound over.

indicators.note: the jumper's word comes after the reworked plea
special treatment of the word plea reworks its letters

parts.note: a frog is a creature famed for its high jumps

explanation.surface: A court case where a high-jumper, after a special plea, is bound over to keep the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges PLEA into LEAP. 'Bound over' looks legal, but it is literally to vault over, as in the playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: The game involves vaulting over a crouching player, so it is literally a bound over someone.

clue.text: Attitude of mind in which one is prepared to strike

definitions.meaning: a position or point of view on an issue

definitions.text: in which one is prepared to strike
definitions.meaning: the batter's or boxer's ready posture before hitting

explanation.surface: A militant mood among workers ready to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: A position taken on an issue, and also the physical posture of a batter or boxer ready to hit.

clue.text: Cut express fare early in the day

parts.note: to break is to cut or interrupt
express means fast, as of a train

explanation.surface: Reduced express rail fares for morning travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a train fare beside 'express', but it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning meal is the food eaten first thing each day.

clue.text: Practised in a small branch

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a branch of an organisation

explanation.surface: Experienced in working within a minor department.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful and proficient through practice, so expert.

clue.text: Witness among Lord's supporters, perhaps

definitions.meaning: spectators at a Test match, as held at Lord's, the London cricket ground

explanation.surface: A witness seated in the crowd of fans at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground where international Test matches are played; its supporters are 'at Test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To certify or bear witness to something, and split in two it places one at a cricket Test match.

clue.text: It's not practical to penalize page in paper

parts.note: to fine someone is to penalize them

indicators.note: the page goes inside the paper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A complaint that punishing a page in a newspaper is unworkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun extremely fine, so over-subtle and too delicate for real use.

clue.text: Special car excited the staff

parts.note: hot means excited or aroused
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: The staff get thrilled about an unusual car.
explanation.definitionFit: A modified vehicle tuned for speed is a customised automobile.

clue.text: Neat sort of sweater for a sailing-vessel

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy
an Aran is a chunky knitted jumper from the Aran Islands

explanation.surface: A tidy jumper to wear aboard a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aran is a thick cable-knit wool jumper from the islands off Ireland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat with three parallel hulls is a type of sailing craft.

clue.text: A celebration for the troops

parts.note: troops here are scout troops, who gather at a large festive rally

explanation.surface: A party thrown for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troops' suggests soldiers, but scouts are organised in troops too, and their big international gathering has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A large gathering of scouts is a festive rally.

clue.text: Restricted to single subject, with no chance of passing

definitions.meaning: obsessive, able to think of only one thing
a railway with a single line, where trains cannot overtake

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded student who will never pass the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a mind fixed on one thing, and literally a single railway line with no overtaking.

clue.text: Reflective, unlike Henry VIII, for example

definitions.meaning: a slender monarch, the opposite of the famously stout Tudor

explanation.surface: Thoughtful, in contrast to a certain Tudor monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry VIII was famously fat, so a slim ruler is a 'thin king'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deep in thought is contemplative, and split it is a slender monarch.

clue.text: Warning upset cricket side

parts.note: to tip is to overturn or upset
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: An alert that a cricket team has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is divided into the off side and the leg (on) side.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint or secret alert given in advance.

clue.text: To break off talking can be an obsession

definitions.meaning: end a phone call by replacing the receiver

explanation.surface: Stopping a conversation can become a fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a phone call, and also a psychological hang-over or fixation.

clue.text: To catch up, runs North to South, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the word for catch from bottom to top

parts.note: to entrap is to catch
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Trying to catch up with a runner heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ENTRAP into PARTNE. In bridge, North and South play as a pair against East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the player seated North is the teammate of South.

clue.text: Sporting companion gambling to finish game

parts.note: play means gamble, as in play the horses
checkmate ends a chess game

explanation.surface: A fellow sportsman betting on the result to end the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend to frolic and play with is a fun-loving companion.

clue.text: Beat rising with volunteer troops in republic

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising reads the word from the bottom up

parts.note: lam means to beat or thrash
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers rising up in a rebellion against a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LAM into MAL. The Territorial Army (TA) was Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island nation became a republic in 1974.

clue.text: Final decision-maker tried changing nothing internally

indicators.note: the zero is placed within the reworked word
changing the word tried reshapes its letters

parts.note: O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: The ultimate authority tried but changed nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges TRIED into EDITR, and 'internally' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper has the last word on what is printed.

clue.text: Start of the endless free draw

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word the
the word for free loses its last letter

parts.note: empty means free, unoccupied

explanation.surface: The beginning of a free-for-all draw with no end.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or entice someone is to attract them.

clue.text: Accountant brought in by partners to conduct scrutiny

indicators.note: the accountant is placed inside the partners

parts.note: in bridge, South and North are partners
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Business partners hire an accountant to audit the books.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South form a partnership, so 'partners' gives S and N; CA (chartered accountant) goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine closely.

clue.text: Easily damaged basket

definitions.meaning: a rush basket used for figs or raisins

explanation.surface: A delicate wicker basket.
explanation.definitionFit: Means fragile, and also an old word for a rush basket for dried fruit.

clue.text: Last person to run branch or manage section

indicators.note: a section is a slice taken from the run of words

explanation.surface: Who last runs the branch or manages the department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' suggests managing a business, but this is the final runner of a relay team.
explanation.definitionFit: The last runner in a relay team is the team's anchor.

clue.text: Car's time still the record here

definitions.text: Car's time still the record here

parts.words: Car's time still the record here
parts.note: a roadside device logs how long a vehicle stays stationary

explanation.surface: A car's lap time remains the record at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' and 'record' suggest motor racing, but this device records how long a car stays still.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated roadside device records paid time for a stationary vehicle.
